correctness.rationale: For \(1<q<2\), set \(r=q/(q-1)>2\). Clarkson's sharp inequality and the two-coordinate norm comparison \(A^2+B^2\le2^{1-2/r}(A^r+B^r)^{2/r}\) combine to give \(\|u+v\|_q^2+\|u-v\|_q^2\le2(\|u\|_q^q+\|v\|_q^q)^{2/q}\). Applying this first to \(u=\lambda x,v=(1-\lambda)y\) and then to \(u=x,v=y\) yields the claimed upper bound. Distinct coordinate unit vectors have disjoint supports and attain equality in both bounds. The endpoint \(q=1\) follows separately from the triangle inequality and the same witness; \(\lambda=0,1\) are included without singularity.
